trees.title: The car pulls to one side
trees.summary: While driving straight, without touching the wheel, the car drifts right or left.
trees.safety: A strong pull that appears only when braking, or a pull that keeps getting worse, needs careful driving to the garage — not driving as normal.

n1.q: When does the car pull to one side?

options.label: Always when driving straight, even without braking
Only on a wet road or in rain

n2.q: Have you checked the tyre air pressure — is there a difference between the sides?

options.label: The pressure is about equal on both sides
After hitting a deep pothole or a kerb

n4.q: Are the tyres on both sides of the car the same model and roughly the same wear?

options.label: No — only one tyre was replaced, or there's a noticeable wear difference
Yes, the same type and roughly the same wear

n5.q: Is the pulling also accompanied by vibration in the steering wheel when braking?

options.label: No, just pulling, sometimes also a noise
Yes, there's also vibration in the wheel

r-tyre-tread-pull.result: Pulling only on a wet road — suspected worn or mismatched tyre
r-tyre-tread-pull.text: Pulling that appears only in rain or on a wet road, and disappears when dry, points to a difference between the tyres in their ability to clear water — one tyre more worn than the other side, or tyres of different models.
actions: Check the tread depth on all the tyres and compare between the sides.
Go to a tyre garage to replace or rotate the tyres as needed.

r-tyre-pressure-pull.result: A difference in tyre air pressure
r-tyre-pressure-pull.text: Lower air pressure on one side creates higher rolling resistance on that side, and the car pulls towards it.
actions: Inflate all the tyres to the pressure set by the car's manufacturer (on the driver's door or in the owner's manual).
If the pulling continues even after fixing it, go and check the wheel alignment.

r-alignment-pull.text: Constant pulling to one side, when the air pressure is normal and equal, points to wheel angles that have gone out of alignment — usually after hitting a deep pothole, a kerb, or from natural wear over time.
actions: Go to a garage for a check and wheel alignment.
Incorrect wheel alignment also wears tyres faster than normal.

r-mismatched-tyres.result: Suspected difference between the tyres on the two sides
r-mismatched-tyres.text: Tyres of different models, or with very different wear, between the two sides of the same axle, can cause pulling even without a real mechanical problem.
actions: Match the tyres on the same axle, and prefer an identical pair.
If the pulling continues after matching them, also check the wheel alignment.

r-caliper-stuck.result: Suspected stuck caliper — a brake that isn't releasing on one side
r-caliper-stuck.text: Pulling only when braking, sometimes with a noise, points to a caliper that isn't releasing properly on one side — the brake on that side keeps pressing slightly even without pressing the pedal, which also generates heat and wears the tyre.
actions: Drive with maximum care to the nearest garage.
If you smell burning from the wheel, stop and check before continuing.

r-warped-disc-pull.result: Pulling and vibration together — suspected uneven brake disc
r-warped-disc-pull.text: Pulling accompanied by vibration in the steering wheel when braking points to a brake disc that has warped or worn unevenly — usually on just one side.
actions: Go to a garage for a check, and to have the disc skimmed or replaced.
For more detail: [[tree:vibration|vibration in the car]].
